proofs.label: a different padlock
reasons: Couldn't confirm this is the same padlock. Both are old dark brown iron padlocks with a thick arched shackle, but the bodies do not match. Photo A shows a complex layered body with side projections and large circular holes on the left and right plus lower holes, and a rivet detail near the shackle. Photo B shows a plain solid rectangular block with no holes, projections or rivet. Neither photo shows the back gate or other surroundings. The structural difference means it cannot be confirmed as the same physical padlock.

proofs.label: a new photo of the same clock
reasons: Couldn't confirm this is the same clock. Both images show the same model of tower clock: glass dome on top, white round dial with black Roman numerals, brass collar below the glass, tapered wooden column, octagonal wooden base with a central gold floral mount, and brass ball feet. However the unique identifiers do not match. The wood tone and grain on the tapered column and on the base panels is dark and plain in Photo A versus lighter with visible swirled burl figure in Photo B, and the gold mount detail looks different. No hall wall or surroundings are visible in either to confirm location. Therefore it cannot be confirmed as the same physical object.
